              ORDER ON ZOOM PROTOCOL AND EXHIBIT EXCHANGE

       THIS MATTER comes before the Hearing Examiners upon their own motion. The

Hearing Examiners have determined that the public hearing in this case shall be held via Zoom

video conferencing platform. Consequently, it is necessary to identify procedures for the remote

sharing of hearing exhibits and to ensure that the hearing is efficient and successful.

       IT IS THERFORE ORDERED:

               A.      Zoom Invitation: An invitation to the Zoom hearing will be circulated via

e-mail to the parties listed in the Official Service List. That invitation can be provided to party

witnesses and all others that the party relies upon for support during the hearing, e.g., an IT

Department or paralegals. The invitation is not to be shared with any people who are not parties

or who will not be participating in the hearing or with people not directly assisting the parties and

counsel with hearing related logistics.

               B.      Attendance at the Hearing: All attorneys and witnesses appearing via Zoom

at the hearing must appear by video. These individuals will not be permitted to utilize audio-only

connections unless necessitated by unexpected technological problems. Each party should ensure

that its participants in the hearing have both audio and video access. The attorneys for each party

shall be responsible for ensuring that each party’s witnesses have sufficient internet access,

microphones, speakers, and familiarity with the Zoom platform to ensure the effective

participation of all witnesses. Any party who fails to ensure that their witness has adequate internet
                BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Zoom Protocol and Exhibit Exchange               Docket No. 25-00079-UT


access and technological tools needed to participate in the Zoom hearing may forfeit their right to

participate. A party’s unfamiliarity with Zoom and videoconferencing technology will not be

permitted to delay or otherwise interfere with the proceeding.

                C.      Livestream: The Zoom hearing will be livestreamed on YouTube. A link to

the livestream will be provided on the Commission’s website at https://www.prc.nm.gov/public-

hearings/. Any person not participating in the hearing as an attorney or witness may view the

hearing through the livestream. Notice of the hearing is also posted on the Commission’s website.

                D.      Uploading Exhibits to Dropbox: By 1:00 p.m. MT on Friday, July 10,

2026, each party will upload to Dropbox (A) each exhibit the party will seek to admit into evidence

at the hearing and (B) an exhibit list identifying all of the party’s exhibits in simple, list form. The

Hearing Examiners will provide instructions for uploading documents via Dropbox in a subsequent

e-mail.

                E.      Exhibit Numbering and Formatting: Exhibits must be identified using

numbers. All files uploaded shall have the following naming convention and format: [Party Name

(Abbreviated)]_[Exhibit Number]_[Testimony Type]_[Last Name of Witness]_[Corrected

Version # (if necessary)]. To illustrate: “SPS_Ex. 2_Direct Testimony_Lees_Corrected 1.” All

documents uploaded must be in .pdf format. Exhibits with colored pages shall retain coloring. Any

document not supplied in the manner just specified shall be admitted into evidence only if the

Hearing Examiners, in their discretion, find good cause to do so.

                F.      Downloading One Another’s Exhibits from Dropbox: Once the parties have

uploaded documents to Dropbox, the Hearing Examiners will share a link allowing parties to

download all documents uploaded.

                G.      Exhibit Corrections: It is unnecessary for any party to seek to correct minor

spelling and grammatical errors discovered on prefiled documents, and parties are discouraged

from offering these types of corrections. The documents uploaded to Dropbox and which parties

will seek to admit at the hearing should include only those corrections that could produce

meaningful confusion about substantive concerns. If any such corrections are necessary, the

witness sponsoring the prefiled testimony that includes the corrections shall identify each

correction verbally at the hearing before his or her testimony is moved into evidence. The Hearing

Examiners reserve the right to reject corrections.

               H.       References to Exhibits at Hearing: All references to exhibits at the hearing

shall be to the exhibit uploaded and then shared with all parties on Dropbox. This will eliminate

or minimize confusion about which version of an exhibit a party is referencing.

                I.      All prefiled testimony of a witness shall be moved into evidence when the

witness is first presented.

                J.      When a witness testifies, the witness shall have readily available during

questioning his or her prefiled testimonies and any documents that a party has indicated will be

the subject of questions for that witness to expedite questioning.

                K.      All attorneys and witnesses shall have readily available all exhibits and

documents shared on Dropbox.

                L.      Attorneys are free to utilize Zoom’s screen-share function during

examination of witnesses and are encouraged to do so to the extent utilizing this function will

facilitate efficient questioning and discussion of admissible documents. Any technical delays

produced by lack of familiarity with the controls in Zoom will be counted against the attorney’s

total cross-examination time. If it becomes clear that an attorney’s lack of familiarity with Zoom
                                            -3-
               BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order on Zoom Protocol and Exhibit Exchange              Docket No. 25-00079-UT


controls slows rather than expedites the proceeding, the Hearing Examiners reserve the right to

take necessary action to ensure the proceeding moves forward with maximum efficiency including

precluding further use of screen sharing or any other Zoom function.

               M.      The oral testimony elicited by the party presenting a witness will (except

for redirect examination) consist of authentication and verification of each prefiled document. The

party will not elicit oral summaries of prefiled testimony or other oral direct testimony.

               N.      Only one attorney for each party shall examine or cross-examine each

witness. The attorney stating objections, if any, during direct examination, shall be the attorney

recognized for cross-examination.

               O.      To make an objection at the hearing, attorneys will state “objection” and

wait to be recognized by the Hearing Examiners before proceeding to state the basis of the

objection. The party whose question is being objected to will cease questioning when an objection

is made and will await guidance from the Hearing Examiners.

               P.      With one limited exception, only counsel presenting the witness may make

objections during cross-examination of that witness. The limited exception is that the Hearing

Examiners will entertain appropriately lodged objections to friendly cross-examination made by

counsel not sponsoring the witness.

               Q.      Friendly cross-examination is prohibited unless authorized by the Hearing

Examiners. Friendly cross-examination entails examining a witness by a party who does not

disagree with the witnesses’ position on the issue. Counsel violating this rule are advised that the

Hearing Examiners may curtail, reduce, or eliminate the remaining cross-examination time of

counsel attempting to engage in friendly cross-examination.

               R.      Commissioners attending the hearing are free to ask questions of witnesses

at a time that is maximally efficient for the commissioner during the time scheduled for that

witness. Following all cross-examination of a witness, the Hearing Examiners may ask questions

of the witness. The Hearing Examiners may also ask questions at other times.

               S.      The scope of redirect-examination is matters arising from cross-

examination and questioning by a commissioner or the Hearing Examiners. The scope of recross-

examination is matters arising from redirect-examination and questioning by the commissioner or

the Hearing Examiners.

               T.      The Hearing Examiners, may at their discretion, limit the time for providing

direct testimony or cross-examination at any public hearing if necessary to promote the proper and

orderly management of such public hearing. 1.2.2.32(G)(3) NMAC.

               U.      Appearances will be taken at the beginning of the evidentiary hearing, and

requests for excusal from the evidentiary hearing or any part of it will be addressed at that time.

       ISSUED under the seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, on July 9, 2026.
